newsitem.title: LEBANON: Amnesty International wants Beirut unionist free.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty International wants Beirut unionist free.

text.p: Amnesty International called on Thursday for the release of leftist labour leader Elias Abou Rizk, who was arrested last week on charges of falsely claiming to head Lebanon's General Labour Confederation (CGTL).

Abou Rizk, a longtime adversary of billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, was arrested after elections in April split the labour movement and produced rival CGTL leaderships headed by himself and Ghneim al-Zoghbi.
The government recognised Zoghbi and state prosecutors subsequently arrested Abou Rizk on charges brought by Zoghbi that he impersonated him as CGTL leader and forcibly usurped office.
The arrest has brought widespread protests in Lebanon from political parties, labour unions and opposition politicians.

"Amnesty International considers Elias Abou Rizk to be a prisoner of conscience, detained for his non-violent activities as a labour leader," Amnesty said in a fax to President Elias Hrawi, Prime Minister Hariri and Justice Minister Bahij Tabbara.
The fax said: "The organisation is calling for his immediate and unconditional release."
It questioned the legality of Abou Rizk's arrest under articles of the penal code carrying at least seven years imprisonment.

"Amnesty International is concerned at the legality of this arrest, particularly the applicability of articles 306 and 392 of the Penal Code which deal with impersonating and usurping civil and military authorities," it said.

A prosecutor filed new charges against Abou Rizk and fellow unionist Yasser Nehme on Wednesday for saying in letters to the International Labour Organisation that Abou Rizk had received death threats.
They were charged with publicising news abroad that undermines Lebanon's reputation -- an offence carrying at least six months jail. Nehme was released pending further investigations.
